💡 Key Takeaways
  • With snow already falling in the Rockies and a strong El Niño weather pattern expected to benefit certain US mountain regions, skiers and riders are already dusting off their gear and booking their winter trips.
  • In a recent development, of course, skiing and snowboarding aren’t typically budget-friendly sports.
  • But in recent years, the industry has moved away from one-day lift tickets in favor of multi-mountain ski passes with heavily discounted rates and additional perks, like Epic’s “Pay Over Time” or Ikon’s deals on friends and family tickets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With snow already falling in the Rockies and a strong El Niño weather pattern expected to benefit certain US mountain regions, skiers and riders are already dusting off their gear and booking their winter trips.

In a recent development, of course, skiing and snowboarding aren’t typically budget-friendly sports. Once you factor in meals, lodging, and transportation in addition to a lift ticket (which costs well over $300 per day at several US resorts), it’s almost worth taking out a loan to pay for a one-week family ski trip.

But in recent years, the industry has moved away from one-day lift tickets in favor of multi-mountain ski passes with heavily discounted rates and additional perks, like Epic’s “Pay Over Time” or Ikon’s deals on friends and family tickets.

The dreamy Major Bear Resort is included on Ikon Pass.

Recent findings suggest that "For those who ski or ride more than six to eight days a season, multi-mountain passes have reshaped the [ski] resort industry,” states Olivia Rowan, publisher of trade magazine Ski Area Management. “The multi-mountain pass opened up new possibilities for snow sports travel and tourism beyond your home hill. They're a great deal for an in-the-know skier or rider.”.

Before choosing a pass, determine your skiing goals for the season. If you’re looking to check out a handful of fresh resorts for a day or two each, the Indy Pass might be your best option. But if you’re hoping to spend a week at a more popular resort like Park City, the Epic or Ikon passes are the way to go. To figure out which pass is best for you and your travel prepares, here's a breakdown of the major players.

Best for: Individuals and families who want unlimited access to some of the world's largest and most popular ski areas.

When the Vail-owned Epic Pass debuted in 2008, it was the first of its kind and set the stage for the multi-mountain passes that followed in the coming years. Today, it remains one of the biggest players in the industry, offering access to over 90 resorts in North America, Europe, Japan, and Australia.

Pricing: The standard Epic Pass, which offers unlimited access to all its resorts, costs $1,169. But if you don’t strategy to ski during holiday weeks and weekends, consider the Epic Local Pass, which excludes peak dates at certain resorts. Epic also offers a customizable pass that lets skiers choose up to 7 days across different resort tiers. The cheapest option, at $337, gives skiers 7 days at 22 resorts in the Midwest, Northeast, and Mid-Atlantic.

Epic Pass offers access to over 90 resorts in North America, Europe, Japan, and Australia.

Vail, Colorado, one of the most popular mountains included with Epic Pass.

Where to visit with the Epic Pass:.

Traveler-approved ski resorts near Epic Pass mountains:.

Best for: Skiers and riders who want to check out several uncrowded, under-the-radar ski resorts.

The Indy Pass, which is the antithesis of larger passes like Epic and Ikon, offers two days of skiing at each of its over 300 partner resorts across four continents. The pass partners with smaller, independently owned resorts that are typically uncrowded and have deeply rooted local vibes. This season, Indy is rolling out an upgrade that lets passholders ski up to five days at 13 resorts, starting at $199. The pass sells out quickly and is already off sale for the 2026-27 ski season, but now is the time to get on the waiting list for next season (sales sometimes reopen mid-season, too).

Pricing: The Indy+ Pass, which doesn’t have blackout dates, costs $469 for adults and $299 for kids 12 and under.

Jay Peak mountain resort in Vermont, which saw record snowfall last winter.

Where to visit with the Indy Pass:.

Traveler-approved ski resorts near Indy Pass mountains:.

Best for: Skiers who live near one of Ikon’s premier destinations, or families with children who want to take advantage of Ikon’s discounted kids passes.

In a recent development, like the Epic Pass, the Ikon Pass offers unlimited access to some of the world’s most popular ski resorts. The pass includes access to over 70 resorts across 13 countries, including some bigger US destinations like Jackson Hole, Deer Valley, and Aspen Snowmass.

Pricing: Like Epic, Ikon offers tiered passes, with its unlimited pass starting at $1,529 (or $1,129 for young adults ages 13-22 and $499 for children ages 5-12). The base pass, which has some blackout dates, starts at $1,099 for adults over 23. Skiers and riders who want to dip their toes into the sport or who may not have time to get out much during the season should consider a personalized pass that allows two, three, or four days at partner resorts.

Fresh powder at Big Bear Mountain Resort, a gem of a mountain on the Ikon Pass.

Where to visit with the Ikon Pass:.

Traveler-approved ski resorts near Ikon Pass mountains:.

Best for: East Coast skiers and riders who mostly plan on skiing in the Mid-Atlantic, Northeast, or eastern Canada, or individuals looking to supplement another multi-mountain pass; It includes two mountains in Colorado and Wyoming, but they are on the smaller side.

New for the 2026-27 ski season, the Snow Pass is the newest player in the game. Like Indy, the Snow Pass offers two days at each partner resort, but so far it has only 14 resorts to choose from, most of which are in the Northeast. You can buy additional days for 30% off the retail price. Snow Pass offers an alternate three-day pass—Snow Triple Play—that includes three days total at 23 partner resorts.

Pricing: The Snow Pass costs $379.99, and the Snow Triple Play costs $189.99.

Whiteface Mountain Ski Resort is a haven of varied terrain for skiers and snowboarders alike.

Where to visit with the Snow Pass:.

Traveler-approved ski resorts near Snow Pass mountains:.

Best for: Skiers and riders who want to check some significant-name resorts off their list but aren’t looking to ski for an extended period at one ski area, or those looking to supplement another multi-mountain or season pass.

Industry observers note that the Mountain Collective Pass offers passholders two days each at its 27 resorts in the US, Canada, Japan, Europe, South America, Australia, and Latest Zealand. It’s a slightly more affordable alternative to the Epic and Ikon, yet it still gives skiers access to big-name resorts like Jackson Hole and Big Sky.

Pricing: The Mountain Collective Pass goes for $729 for adults, $594 for teens, and $304 for kids 6-12. Skiers and riders who want to ski more than their allotted 2 days at a specific resort can purchase day tickets at half off.

A sprawling mountain view at Jackson Hole, included on the Mountain Collective pass.

Where to visit with the Mountain Collective Pass:.

#42448. Independents decide the election, again!

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1180 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

Independents decide the election, again!

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1180 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that A group of fresh senators-elect gather for a photo in Minority Leader Charles E.
  • Once more, independents were the decisive factor in what amounts to the Republicans’ midterm disaster that was both broad and deep.
  • “We hired you to fix the Biden economy and you failed.” Pretty simple.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A group of fresh senators-elect gather for a photo in Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer’s office in Washington on Monday. The large class of incoming Democratic senators was propelled by votes from independents, Winston writes. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

Once more, independents were the decisive factor in what amounts to the Republicans’ midterm disaster that was both broad and deep. No one who reads this column should have been surprised that this growing segment of the electorate became the equivalent of the “deciders-in-chief” who used their vote to send a tough message to the president and his party.

“We hired you to fix the Biden economy and you failed.” Pretty simple.

According to the exit polls, Democrats won independents by an astonishing 22 points. If this holds, it will be the largest margin in the history of exit polling, beating the Republican margin in 2010 of 19 points. For Republicans, this is the fifth consecutive election losing independents.

It was the size of the GOP defeat with independents that put the number of states and congressional districts into play, districts that President Donald Trump won in 2024, many by double digits.

Industry observers note that independents made up 33 percent of the electorate; Democrats were at 35 percent and Republicans at 32 percent. This is the second consecutive election where independents were a larger part of the electorate than one of the major parties. It also reveals that while independents may not have been enthused about voting, they showed up.

Looking at the 13 battleground Senate races, which now include Mississippi, Democrats won independents in all of them by double digits, and 10 of them by 20 points or more. The independent vote allowed Democrats to overwhelm significant Republican Party ID advantages in many red states and districts.

For example, in Kansas (exit poll not final), Republicans had a 17-point party advantage, but lost independents by 33. Incumbent Sen. Roger Marshall went down with a 5-point loss. In South Carolina, Republicans had a 14-point party advantage, but lost independents by 31 points. A liberal activist Democrat beat a neophyte Republican candidate, appointed Sen. Darline Graham, by 4 points.

Despite Texas Republicans’ 5-point party ID advantage, Ken Paxton lost independents by 31 points and lost the Senate race by a huge 12 points. It goes without saying that voters in Texas shocked Republicans by not only rejecting the president’s primary choice for Senate, but taking down all Republicans in statewide races.

Recent findings suggest that overall, Republicans lost six states with key Senate races where Trump won by double digits in 2024, with Mississippi being a potential seventh. In the House (with 7 races yet to be called at the time of this writing), Democrats have won 56 congressional districts that Trump carried in 2024, along with carrying all 201 districts that Harris won.

According to recent reports, clearly, Republican operatives, consultants and the media missed the boat when it came to evaluating the viability of House races. Using the 2024 Trump-Harris race results to assess the safety or vulnerability of a particular seat proved to be the wrong context.

In the spring, I was beginning to see some danger signals in our polling and in public surveys that raised questions for me about just how many House seats were actually in play, fearing perhaps far more than anyone was predicting. By early summer, I decided to undertake a different analysis on the state of current races using the 2020 Trump-Biden results by congressional district. The research found a much larger number of GOP seats could be vulnerable. In the end, the analysis proved to be right. Democrats won all of the 220 districts that Biden carried, and at least 37 seats that Trump won.

According to the exit polls, the independent vote, not surprisingly, was largely driven by the economy, their top issue concern. Much to the detriment of Trump and the Republicans, 80 percent of independents thought the economy was not good/poor, versus 20 percent who thought the economy was excellent/good. In terms of inflation, 82 percent said it had been a severe or moderate hardship for them, and 89 percent said the cost of living was a crucial or major factor in how they voted for Congress.

Sources indicate that the president and his party got the blame. Looking at specific policies, 71 percent of independents thought that Trump’s tariff policies had hurt the national economy, and more broadly, 72 percent said his policies had worsened economic conditions in the country. As a result, Trump’s overall job approval among these voters was 29 percent approve with 71 disapproving; 59 percent strongly disapproving. These extraordinarily bad numbers topped even Biden’s worst job approval numbers.

Recent findings suggest that trump’s decision to ask voters to “pretend I’m on the ballot,” was, in retrospect, a strategic miscalculation. It was a mistake to tell voters that the economy was in great shape when it was clear the majority of people were very unhappy when it came to inflation — the rising cost of gas and groceries.

A little empathy on economic issues and a lot better explanation of why the Iran conflict was crucial to national security and worth the economic sacrifice would have gone a long way to minimizing the size of the GOP defeat.

In a recent development, neither happened, and Republicans were overwhelmed by a blue tsunami almost nobody saw coming. Still, despite the size of the Democrats’ win, they would be wrong to see this as an ideological mandate of any sort. The exit polls revealed that the electorate remains center-right. Moderates are the largest component at 41 percent, but conservatives still outnumber liberals by a 33-26 margin.

Independents have a negative view of both parties. Their view of Republicans is 32 percent favorable and 68 percent unfavorable. However, Democrats are not far behind, at 42 percent favorable and 58 percent unfavorable.

At a policy level when independents were asked which party was better able to handle the economy, 41 percent stated the Democratic Party, 28 percent said the Republican Party, and 30 percent said neither. Both parties are well short of a majority. This reflects the fact that the electorate still negatively remembers the Biden economy, but also believes that Republicans didn’t fix it as they promised two years ago.

According to recent reports, democrats would be wise to moderate and not continue down the increasingly extreme progressive path. Republicans and the president need to take a hard look at their own failings and understand that when it comes to voters, especially independents, all the money in the world is no substitute for good candidates with real solutions.

It has been revealed that david Winston is the president of The Winston Group and a longtime adviser to congressional Republicans. He previously served as the director of planning for Speaker Newt Gingrich. He advises Fortune 100 companies, foundations and nonprofit organizations on strategic planning and public policy issues, as well as serving as an election analyst for CBS News.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Holland America Line has announced that bookings are open for its 2028 Alaska Cruisetour season, giving guests their first opportunity to pair an overland journey into the Great Land with a cruise aboard the reimagined Oosterdam.

The Oosterdam will make its Alaska debut in 2028, bringing latest onboard experiences to a Cruisetour program that combines the coast with deeper exploration into Alaska’s interior.

Guests can choose from 19 Cruisetours itineraries aboard four ships, ranging from nine to 17 days, operating between May and September.

Each experience combines an Alaska cruise with an overland journey that includes a stay at the newly transformed Holland America Denali Lodge, following completion of its $70 million multi-year enhancement project in 2027.

Each Cruisetour also includes a tour into the park and travel through Alaska’s interior by rail and motorcoach, the tech giant mentioned in a press release.

The tech giant added that Classic, Signature and Ultimate Alaska & Denali Cruisetours pair the overland experience with a seven-day Glacier Discovery cruise aboard the Oosterdam or Eurodam, while Alaska, Denali & Yukon Cruisetours travel farther into Canada’s Yukon Territory with either a seven-day Glacier Discovery cruise or a shorter Alaska Inside Passage cruise aboard the Koningsdam or Zaandam.

Holland America Line is the only cruise line to take guests into the Yukon on a Cruisetour, traveling beyond Skagway to Whitehorse and Dawson City.

NASA’s Voyager 1 Makes History Reaching One Light-Day From Earth

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1013 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nasa

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • NASA’s Voyager 1 probe, humanity’s farthest-flying spacecraft, has reached one light-day from Earth, after more than 49 years of constant travel.
  • Voyager team members at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California, managed by Caltech, heard from the probe 24 hours later, the time it took for the spacecraft’s radio signal traveling at the speed of light to reach Earth, early Thursday.
  • “Traveling a light-day is a singular feat for a spacecraft, but Voyager is so much more than a distant traveler.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NASA’s Voyager 1 probe, humanity’s farthest-flying spacecraft, has reached one light-day from Earth, after more than 49 years of constant travel. A light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours, equaling about 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). The spacecraft achieved the milestone at 2:16 a.m. PST (5:16 a.m. EST) Nov. 18.

Voyager team members at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California, managed by Caltech, heard from the probe 24 hours later, the time it took for the spacecraft’s radio signal traveling at the speed of light to reach Earth, early Thursday.

“Traveling a light-day is a singular feat for a spacecraft, but Voyager is so much more than a distant traveler. The Voyager mission would be remarkable just for what it contributed to planetary science with the Grand Tour of the outer planets,” remarked Joe Westlake, director, Heliophysics Division at NASA Headquarters in Washington. “But it went on to become central to NASA’s fleet of heliophysics missions offering insights into the star that we all revolve around, the Sun.”.

According to recent reports, scientists use light to measure the vast distances of space. Light travels at about 186,000 miles (299,000 kilometers) a second in a vacuum. A ray of sunlight passing Earth takes about 1.3 seconds to reach the Moon, about four hours to reach Neptune, and another 20 hours to reach Voyager 1. For comparison, a light-year is 5.88 trillion miles (9.46 trillion kilometers).

Even though the team has not received science and engineering data from Voyager 1 since Nov. 14, the spacecraft is sending what is called a carrier signal, which typically conveys that data to Earth. Mission engineers used the carrier signal and trajectory calculations to confirm the light-day milestone. They continue to analyze the issue impacting the science and engineering data.

Humanity’s only probes in interstellar space, Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2, released in 1977 to take advantage of a rare planetary alignment. Managed by JPL, they were only the third and fourth spacecraft to visit Jupiter and Saturn, and the first to return high-resolution imagery, transforming our understanding of these worlds and their moons. Voyager 2 went on to study the ethereal ice giants, Neptune and Uranus. Both spacecraft continue to measure changes in the Sun’s magnetic field across vast distances.

It has been revealed that “Voyager 1 crossing the light-day threshold is yet another historic feat on an extraordinary voyage of discovery,” said Dave Gallagher, JPL director. “Above all, this milestone stands as a testament to the exceptional teams who built, programmed, and fly these spacecraft today, and who have overcome countless challenges to keep them connected to Earth across the vastness of space. As NASA pushes toward new frontiers in human and robotic exploration, Voyager and the people behind its success continue to inspire us to reach farther and dream bigger.”.

In addition to their suite of scientific instruments, the Voyager probes carry a Golden Record, a gold-plated copper phonograph compiling images and sounds from Earth, as a message to any advanced civilization that might one day find it.

According to recent reports, “Nearly half a century after leaving Earth, the Voyager mission continues to push the boundaries of human exploration. Its epic journey reflects the vision of Ed Stone, the Caltech physicist and JPL director who guided the mission for decades, and the curiosity and tenacity of generations of scientists and engineers who have carried that vision forward,” mentioned Ray Jayawardhana, president, Caltech. “Beyond its immense contributions to science, Voyager also captures something profound about the human spirit. We may never know where its journey will ultimately lead, but it will venture on, an enduring affirmation that humanity was here and we yearned to explore.”.

Sources indicate that traveling about 38,000 mph (61,155 kph), Voyager 1 in 2012 became the first spacecraft to leave the heliosphere, the bubble of particles and magnetic fields created by the Sun that deflects cosmic radiation, and enter interstellar space. Voyager 2, taking a different trajectory, crossed the boundary in 2018.

According to recent reports, “The Voyagers are revolutionizing our understanding of interstellar space, a previously unexplored region outside the heliosphere,” remarked Linda Spilker, Voyager project scientist at JPL. “One significant surprise is the extent to which our Sun continues to affect interstellar space, all the way out to Voyager 1. Where does the Sun’s influence end and pristine interstellar space begin? Perhaps Voyager may endure long enough to answer that question.”.

Creative engineering solutions have enabled the probes to conserve energy and overcome challenges related to aging hardware, including clogged thrusters and a malfunctioning computer on the spacecraft. Earlier this year, engineers successfully turned off three devices on Voyager 1 and substituted them with three lower-power alternatives — a move not without risk — to help the spacecraft make the most of its 50-year-old radioisotope thermal generator. Essentially a nuclear battery, the generator converts heat from decaying plutonium into electricity.

According to recent reports, with the plutonium supply continually depleting, both Voyager probes lose about 4 watts of power each year. The latest energy-saving effort is expected to provide enough power for both spacecraft to keep their current suite of science instruments operating until at least their 50th launch anniversaries next summer.

As with all NASA spacecraft that venture to and beyond the Moon, communication between Earth and the Voyager probes is managed by the agency’s Deep Space Network, large antennas located at three facilities around the world.

“We listen to Voyager 1 every day and send commands to the spacecraft weekly. It just takes a little longer to communicate than it used to,” stated Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager at JPL. “Even traveling at the speed of light, signals now take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft and 24 hours to reach us. One day in the future, when it can no longer communicate with Earth, Voyager 1 will become humanity’s silent ambassador to the stars.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Robert Garcia, D-Calif., is expected to lead the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee.
  • The Trump administration signaled it would respond aggressively to a Democratic-led Congress with a letter this week threatening to prosecute lawmakers for oversight efforts.
  • The letter from White House Counsel Will Scharf sent Monday to House Oversight and Government Reform ranking member Robert Garcia, D-Calif., argued that members of Congress have limited authority to conduct oversight of a presidential administration and that some of the threats to issue subpoenas “may cross the line into blatant criminality.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., is expected to lead the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call file photo).

The Trump administration signaled it would respond aggressively to a Democratic-led Congress with a letter this week threatening to prosecute lawmakers for oversight efforts.

The letter from White House Counsel Will Scharf sent Monday to House Oversight and Government Reform ranking member Robert Garcia, D-Calif., argued that members of Congress have limited authority to conduct oversight of a presidential administration and that some of the threats to issue subpoenas “may cross the line into blatant criminality.”.

In a recent development, the letter, obtained from a White House official, marks the latest escalation from the Trump administration ahead of Democrats taking control of both chambers of Congress next year. It also dovetails with years of Trump’s threats to prosecute his critics.

“We are monitoring the abusive and capricious threats that are now proliferating from Democrat legislators who seek to abuse the legislative process to intimidate and to interfere with the lawful functioning of government,” the letter says.

Garcia, the likely committee chair next Congress, pushed back on the threat in a statement Wednesday, accusing the administration of having “something to hide” and that Congress has wide authority to investigate the executive branch.

“The American people voted overwhelmingly for us to pass laws to root out corruption and abuse," Garcia stated. "The Trump Administration continues to weaponize the government with threats of unconstitutional attacks on Congress. We are a co-equal branch of government and will not be deterred by baseless threats from a weaponized DOJ or from the President’s lawyers.”.

The letter came after Attorney General Todd Blanche previously refused to rule out criminal charges against members of Congress in response to investigations.

"It depends on what the crime is and what they have done,” Blanche told CNN over the weekend.

Last week, President Donald Trump himself remarked that threats of investigations and impeachment were “extortion at the highest level” and called for the Justice Department to “look into this criminal act, immediately!”.

He also singled out Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., calling for her to be imprisoned. The administration previously unsuccessfully attempted to indict Slotkin and other Democrats over a video she published calling for soldiers to disobey illegal orders.

Industry observers note that and Trump last year publicly called for longtime critic Sen. Adam B. Schiff, D-Calif., to face unspecified charges in a post on Truth Social addressed to then-Attorney General Pam Bondi that also called for the prosecution of former FBI Director James Comey and New York Attorney General Letitia James. Both have faced criminal charges, pleaded not guilty and fought them in court as political attacks.

It has been revealed that garcia and other Democrats have signaled they intend to pursue oversight aggressively in the upcoming Congress. After Democrats won the House majority last week, Garcia put out an all-caps statement urging administration officials to “LAWYER UP” ahead of the new year.

Sources indicate that garcia, as well as other likely incoming chairs such as House Judiciary ranking member Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md.; Homeland Security ranking member Rep. Bennie Thompson, D-Miss.; and Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., have hinted at broad inquiries ranging from the handling of files related to deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein to immigration enforcement and more.

Raskin told reporters last week that he thought Democratic oversight efforts could dovetail with the party’s broader effort to address affordability complications, including by addressing the Iran war, allegations of corruption within the Trump administration and more.

“We're going to get all the information that we need in order to restore the rule of law in American constitutional democracy,” Raskin mentioned.

The letter also echoes a previous fight the administration pitched with the House in the first Trump administration, where officials resisted in court allowing former White House Counsel Don McGahn to testify to the House Judiciary Committee for years.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Test teams fired the developmental engine for the planned duration of three minutes and 20 seconds (200 seconds).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NASA tested RS-25 engine No. 10001 on Nov. 18 on the Fred Haise Test Stand at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi.

Test teams fired the developmental engine for the planned duration of three minutes and 20 seconds (200 seconds).

While this developmental engine will not be used in flight, the hot fire test provides NASA and NASA’s prime contractor L3Harris Technologies with the capability to capture critical data to improve engine performance and reliability for future Artemis missions.

For the Artemis IV Moon landing mission in 2028, the SLS rocket will launch astronauts aboard the Orion spacecraft from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. This mission will be a key step in the agency’s broader goals to explore the lunar South Pole, establish an enduring human presence on the lunar surface, and build on the agency’s foundation for the first crewed mission to Mars.

For each Artemis mission, four RS-25 engines produce up to 2 million pounds of combined thrust to help launch the SLS rocket.

Recent findings suggest that all RS-25 engines are tested and proven flightworthy at NASA Stennis prior to use. Tests are conducted by a team of operators from NASA, L3Harris, and Nova Space Solutions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A-Rosa’s Brava will serve as floating accommodation for various events in Germany at the start of 2027.

The cruise line noted in a press release that the ship’s season would be extend by turning it into a stationary hotel ship in Cologne and Düsseldorf in January and February 2027.

Being moored near the Cologne Trade Fair and the Düsseldorf Trade Fair Center, the ship will offer overnight accommodation during several trade fairs and the Carnival season.

The 2011-built ship can accommodate a maximum of 202 guests in 99 cabins.

“The MICE business is an notable and growing segment for us. River cruise ships offer particular advantages here, as their manageable size often allows for centrally located berths. Trade fair and event attendees, as well as business travelers, benefit from short distances and direct access to the event venues,” said Stephanie Schrahe, director of omnichannel sales.

To kick things off, the A-Rosa Brava will be moored in Cologne from January 19-22, 2027, for the Cologne international furniture fair.

Following this, the ship will be docked in Düsseldorf January 23-29, 2027, during the boot Düsseldorf water sports trade fair.

From January 30 to February 3, 2027, the A-Rosa Brava will serve as a hotel in Cologne for visitors to the ISM confectionery trade fair and guests attending the Men’s Handball World Championship final.

Finally, February 3-10, 2027, the ship will welcome guests in Cologne who are there for the Carnival season.

The offer includes a breakfast buffet and is also available for solo travelers.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • This is part of our global guide to the Best Places to Go in 2027—find more travel inspiration here.
  • Go for: a museum boom and a vibrant cultural milieu.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While editing this year’s list, one thing swiftly became very clear: 2027 is poised to be a banner one for cultural experiences across Africa. While chatting with our writers, I kept finding compelling reasons to go back to my favorite corners—the Kigali Triennale’s return to Rwanda in September, Jazzablanca’s 20th anniversary in Casablanca, and an even more vibrant creative landscape in Tunis than the one I reported on six years ago. But now I’m adding Benin to my list, thanks to four—yes, four—eagerly anticipated latest museums debuting in the year ahead that will showcase everything from modern art to critical artifacts recently repatriated from Europe. Elsewhere on the continent there are fresh ways to experience some of its familiar pleasures, owing to a high-end resort boom on the beaches of Zanzibar, a host of safari lodge openings in Zambia, eight new marine reserves in São Tomé and Principe, and a groundbreaking five-country trans-frontier conservation area. Be sure to make some time for rarer incentives to travel too, like a once-in-a-generation “superbloom” in South Africa and the “eclipse of the century” over Luxor, Egypt (it also helps that there are some swish new places to stay at these places).But one of the most endearing stories of an African destination of the past year may be Cape Verde: Is the “World Cup effect” going to bring a wave of curious travelers to the archipelago? Read on to decide for yourself. —Sarah Khan.

This is part of our global guide to the Best Places to Go in 2027—find more travel inspiration here.

Go for: a museum boom and a vibrant cultural milieu.

Home to ancient Kingdom of Dahomey, Benin has transformed into a destination for heritage tourism.

It has been revealed that benin is a place where history runs deep: It’s home to the ancient Kingdom of Dahomey, the spiritual traditions of Vodun, and Ouidah—one of West Africa’s significant ports in the transatlantic slave trade. Now the country is turning that history into a upcoming era of cultural tourism, while creating ways for travelers, particularly people of African descent, to reconnect with their heritage.

Ouidah, an especially key destination for those tracing their ancestry, is central to that effort. In 2025 the government revealed plans to invest $1.4 billion in tourism and cultural development, including for infrastructure, heritage restitution, and indigenous traditions. In 2027 that transformation is expected to become more visible with a host of fresh museum openings, like the Museum of Modern Art in Cotonou; the International Museum of Memory and Slavery in Ouidah; and the Museum of the Epic of the Amazons and Kings of Dahomey in Abomey. The latter of which is expected to house 26 royal artifacts repatriated by France in 2021.

Vodun Days, an eight-day celebration of Benin’s indigenous spiritual traditions taking place January 2–9, 2027, will showcase ceremonies, music, and dance. Meanwhile, Villa Karo in Grand-Popo—a bridge between artists and researchers from Finland, Sweden, and West Africa—will continue its residency program, which brings artists to its seaside research center to connect with the local community through workshops, concerts, and exhibitions. The famous stilt village of Ganvié, meanwhile, remains open to visitors as its Reinventing the Lakeside City of Ganvié project upgrades tourism infrastructure. Benin is also beginning to make appearances on cruise itineraries. Two latest Swan Hellenic sailings in 2027 sailings feature the country, including an April voyage from Luanda to Accra and an October sailing from Ghana to Angola. —Harriet Akinyi.

Go for: beaches, festivals, and new-found buzz.

Newly introduced Cabo Verde Airlines flight routes launched in May 2026, and coupled with the “World Cup effect,” will make travel to Cape Verde more appealing than ever.

According to recent reports, during FIFA World Cup 2026, one of the most impressive performances came from Cape Verde, an archipelago of 10 islands off Africa’s Atlantic Ocean coast. Now the “World Cup effect” has gotten travelers curious about what the destination has to offer. It helps that getting there is easier than ever, thanks to newly introduced direct flights launched in May 2026 from Rhode Island’s T.F. Green International Airport on Cabo Verde Airlines. On the island of Sal, which boasts white-sand beaches and over 350 days of sunshine a year, adrenaline-driving activities range from swimming with lemon sharks to kite- and windsurfing, while those seeking a more relaxed experience can float in the saline pools of Pedra de Lume. The island’s luxury accommodation options are also getting an upgrade with Hyatt Regency Cape Verde Sal as well as a family-friendly all-inclusive Bahia Principe set to open in 2027. In March the 322-room Robinson Boa Vista will welcome its first guests to the easternmost island of Boa Vista, known as the Sahara in the Atlantic due to its desert-like flat plains. São Vicente and Praia are the islands to hit for local music—the samba-inspired São Vicente Carnival features dance performances, fireworks, and floats, while Praia hosts the annual Kriol Jazz Festival and the Atlantic Music Expo. Africa’s first Four Points by Sheraton resort opened in the port city of São Vicente last March, with 105 rooms and 22 suites overlooking either Laginha Beach, known for its turquoise waters, or the Monte Verde mountains. —Mazuba Kapambwe.

Go for: a vibrant cultural and design scene.

Casablanca's 2027 roster of cultural events include the 20th anniversary of Jazzablanca in July and the newly launched Morocco Design fair.

Casablanca stealthily enters 2027 as Africa’s most creative urban reinvention. It’s an apt year to visit, given the pioneering Royal Air Maroc flights, released in June 2026, linking Casablanca with Los Angeles—the first African connection to America's Pacific Coast. It is a poetic bridge, connecting the dream factory that conjured Casablanca’s mythic character with the modern metropolis redefining itself as a vanguard of contemporary Maghrebi culture. A cornerstone of this cultural renaissance is the 20th anniversary of Jazzablanca in July: Once an intimate gathering, it has evolved into North Africa's best boutique music festival, hosting emerging Afrobeat, jazz, and urban artists beneath the modernist skyscrapers in Anfa Park and on stages in the palm-lined Arab League Park beside the Nevada skate park. Design lovers, meanwhile, can admire the Museum of Photography and Visual Arts, which was inaugurated in June in the medina and is Tadao Ando’s sole architectural project on the continent. The museum and the recently launched annual Morocco Design fair, which spotlights high-end design studios, establish Casablanca as an emerging destination for cutting-edge design, music, and art. The city's heritage sites are getting a revamp too. The iconic 1916 Neo-Moorish Lincoln Hotel by Radisson Collection is being masterfully revived by French Moroccan architects OUALALOU + CHOI, who are pairing its historic façade with an über-minimalist interior. From the hotel’s doorstep, a upcoming tramline whisks you to the Casablanca Finance City (CFC), a glittering new commercial district composed of futuristic, climate-resilient buildings that pay homage to Casablanca’s legacy of concrete experimentation. Nearby, bougie restaurants like Le 7ème Ciel draw crowds and a new Radisson Red will open in 2027 to join an existing Radisson Blu. CFC is built on the old Anfa Airport, from which The Little Prince author and architecture school dropout Antoine de Saint-Exupéry flew a perilous mail route to Dakar in an open-cockpit Bréguet 14 biplane, returned for drinks at Le Petit Poucet, and lived with his fiery Salvadorean muse, Consuelo Suncín. Then, as now, the city was a nexus connecting continents and a frontier to the future. —Paula Hardy.

Go for: a ground-breaking cross-border safari project and birding adventure.

The Kavango-Zambezi Transfrontier Conservation Area, or KAZA TFCA, is the world's largest terrestrial transboundary conservation area.

Zambia, which has forgone visa requirements of 53 countries and has increased international flights, will be the center of attention.

In a world where ecological degradation and global discord are reasons to despair, Kavango-Zambezi Transfrontier Conservation Area, or KAZA TFCA, is more rising sun than ray of hope. Supported by five countries—Angola, Botswana, Namibia, Zambia, and Zimbabwe, the world’s largest terrestrial transboundary conservation area encompasses a region roughly the size of France and is watered by the Kavango, Zambezi, Chobe, Kwando, and Kafue river systems. Officially rolled out in 2012, it languished as a proposal on paper for years, but recent initiatives have seen it shake off bureaucratic paralysis: Green Growth for KAZA, the umbrella initiative, directly links community benefits to conservation. Several depleted parks have been rewilded; Africa’s first cross-border avitourism project, the Great Kavango Zambezi Birding Route, was recently launched; and connectivity improved—Shearzone Safari launched a charter service in Zambia in early 2026. Notably, Angola has entered the guided-safari arena with Luiana Plains Expedition Camp, the first to open in the 10.3-million-acre Luengue-Luiana National Park in July 2026. It will soon be followed by Natural Selection, which is developing a new 500,000-acre game reserve around Angola’s existing Cuatir Reserve. In Namibia’s unsung Zambezi Region, Thitake River Lodge opens on the banks of the Kwando in Bwabwara National Park late in 2026, while Nkasa Linyanti is the fabulous new linchpin in Nkasa Rupara National Park. But the KAZA TFCA region that’s experiencing the biggest proliferation is Zambia, buoyed by the scrapping of visa requirements of 53 countries and increased international flights. Ker & Downey launched its Zambia division with King Lewanika Lodge in remote Liuwa Plains National Park, the first luxury base from which to witness Africa’s second-largest wildebeest migration; its second location, Musesenji River Camp, opens in April 2027. And luring the well-heeled to 5.5-million-acre Kafue National Park are Anantara with Tented Camp Kafue River, and Classic Zambia with new Lwenge River Camp; both opened this summer. —Pippa de Bruyn.

Go for: a wave of gallery and festival openings turning a gorilla trek stopover into an art capital.

Kigali's art scene is ramping up as institutions like Kigali Triennial and Gihanga Institute of Contemporary Art platform Rwandan and East African artists.

Fresh Kigali properties are showcases for art, such as the nine-room Pinnacle hotel and members' club.

For years Kigali has been seen as little more than a pit stop before going gorilla trekking. Now the city is making a compelling case for staying awhile. The city’s vibrant food and fashion have already been putting it on the map, and now the art scene is getting noticed as several institutions build platforms for championing Rwandan and East African artists. September 2027 marks the second edition of the Kigali Triennial, which is primed to rival some of the continent’s more established art festivals, like ART X Lagos and Dak'Art Biennale. The Gihanga Institute of Contemporary Art, which opened at the end of 2025, highlights artists from across Africa and its diasporas, with a focus on East Africa with two exhibitions: “Space Encounters,” exploring human connection and memory, which is currently on through December 2026; and a collection of contemporary work by Sudanese artists opening in January 2027. This follows the debut of the Inyuguti Art Hub this year, which brought together 19 artists from across Africa and the UK, including Rwandan Elisa Niyogisubizo (also the gallery’s founder), Burundi-based Peter Kamale, and Nigerian Pascal Ejiofor. The lines between the art and hotel scenes are beginning to blur too, with a upcoming generation of properties doubling as cultural showcases. Among them is the nine-room Pinnacle hotel and members club that opened in early 2026 as Rwanda’s first women-led ultraluxury boutique property, showcasing the owner’s private art collection. Creative events are rippling beyond the capital, as Rwandan artists Willy Karekezi and Cedric Mizero are each launching new spaces in Musanze, the gateway town for gorilla trekking, in 2027: Karekezi will open a residency alongside his Indiba Arts Space in Kigali, and Mizero will open Umugenzi, an addition to the multisite Ikinyugunyugu art residency. —Vivienne Dovi.

Go for: the eclipse of the century and nostalgia-soaked Nile cruises.

Astrotourism is coming for Luxor and the Nile on August 2, 2027, thanks to the six-minute “eclipse of the century" and a wave of latest boats promising prime viewing spots along the ancient waterway.

According to recent reports, dubbed the eclipse of the century, 2027’s much-anticipated celestial event will reach its zenith in Luxor, Egypt, on August 2, when the moon will block out the sun for a record-breaking 6 minutes and 23 seconds. Fitting, perhaps, for a place where the mystical has always loomed large, the mountains hold secret treasures, the temples and tombs have been perfectly preserved roughly 3,000 years after they were built, and the Nile exudes a life force of its own. Travelers have come to this transcendent stretch of Upper Egypt, nearly 400 miles south of Cairo, for millennia. Luxor itself served as Egypt’s capital from 1570 BCE to 1069 BCE, but today is better known as the home of the Valley of the Kings, and the start or end point of nostalgia-infused Nile cruises to and from Aswan, a leisurely four- or five-day sail away. Both destinations are primed for a momentous 2027: In Luxor the much-loved Winter Palace—archaeologist Howard Carter’s base during his 1922 Tutankhamen tomb discovery—will reopen in July as a Mandarin Oriental after an extensive renovation exactly 120 years after its official inauguration. Aswan’s own grande dame, the Old Cataract, which famously inspired Agatha Christie’s best-selling novel Death on the Nile, has also been taken over by Mandarin Oriental and will reopen its Nile Wing in 2027 after a thorough upgrade. Mandarin Oriental will launch its first Nile cruise that connects the two, joining a flurry of other upcoming boats taking to the ancient waterway. Among them the Oberoi Melouk and the Oberoi Malekat dahabiyas, with only seven cabins apiece, and homegrown operator Kemetale’s second boat, Deshret, with its Nile-view sauna, plunge pool, and spa treatments. —Selina Denman.

Go for: a rare ‘superbloom’ of endemic flora and world-class wines at Africa’s southern tip.

Cape Agulhas, Africa's southernmost tip, offers a new interpretation center focused on the history and geology of Agulhas, as well as a 177-year-old lighthouse.

Chef Michael Broughton, formerly of Terroir in Stellenbosch, now leads the kitchen at historic Fisherman’s Cottage, putting seafood centerstage.

Sources indicate that cape Town. Winelands. Then head off on safari. That’s the typical circuit for travelers jetting into South Africa. But in 2027 look beyond to the Overberg—“over mountain” in Afrikaans—region, where wildfires have triggered a floral extravaganza not seen in decades. Base yourself in Hermanus for memorable whale watching from the seven-and-a-half-mile Cliff Path. The Marine Hotel, a seafront landmark since 1902, has unveiled a fynbos-inspired revamp of its public spaces and seafood-driven Pavilion Restaurant. There’s a newly introduced culinary energy in town too: Chef Michael Broughton, previously at Terroir in Stellenbosch, has turned the historic Fisherman’s Cottage into a hotbed of polished Cape coastal cuisine (don’t miss the spaghetti aglio e olio with local rock lobster). Broughton’s wine list leans into estates from the nearby Hemel-en-Aarde (Heaven and Earth) valley, where cellars are known for exceptional Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. Creation Wines offers a new sculpture-led vineyard walk, and opens a private tasting room in May 2027 aimed at wine lovers looking for a deep dive into the cool-climate terroir. Bouchard Finlayson, one of the oldest estates in the valley, reopens in late 2027 after an extensive renovation, with a new tasting space and art collection.

Industry observers note that set in the heart of the Cape Floristic Region, Grootbos Private Nature Reserve is a biodiversity hot spot. Wildfires that swept the area in 2025 sparked a superbloom of latest growth, including dormant species that haven’t flowered in decades like wild orchids and the fire-dependent Gladiolus overbergensis. Guided botanical walks and drives get you in the thick of the fynbos, but a new equestrian center also makes this a great choice for horse-riding holidays. Long popular with families, Coot Club, on the nearby Klein River Lagoon, expands in 2027 with a pair of new two-bedroom boathouses and brings a new wellness focus with outdoor yoga sessions and in-room wellness treatments. Toast it all with a sundowner in the refreshed Flamingo Bar upstairs in the original homestead. An hour’s drive east, Cape Agulhas, the southernmost tip of Africa, is a fitting finale. A new interpretation center delves into the history and geology of Agulhas, after which you can climb the 177-year-old lighthouse and stand on the rocky shoreline where the Indian and Atlantic Oceans meet. —Richard Holmes.

Go for: new marine reserves and World Heritage Sites.

Often known as the African Galapagos for its high concentration of endemic species, the island nation of São Tomé and Principe is surrounded by clear waters full of manta rays, sharks, and migrating humpback whales.

In a recent development, on the islands of São Tomé and Príncipe, more than 155 miles off the coast of Gabon in the Gulf of Guinea, a thick rainforest punctuated by needle-like rock formations meets shores of white and volcanic black sand. One of the world’s least visited countries, and known as the African Galapagos for its high concentration of endemic species, this island nation is surrounded by clear turquoise waters brimming with manta rays and reef and nurse sharks. Humpback whales migrate through seasonally, and turtles begin to nest on the beaches in November before hatching between February and April. In 2025 the first two of eight newly introduced dedicated marine reserves, Santana and Ilhéu das Rolas, were approved; in 2026, six roças, or former Portuguese plantations, were designated UNESCO World Heritage Sites, recognized for their role in shaping the social, economic, and cultural history of the nation, which was once the world’s preeminent supplier of cacao. Two of these roças are a part of the Príncipe Collection—the hospitality arm of sustainable development group HBD Príncipe—meaning you can stay at these historically significant sites. One of the properties on offer is Hotel Belo Monte, which opened in June and sits high up on a hillside overlooking the rainforest and sea. A stay in this eco-hideaway, chicly styled with splashes of bold color, comes with cultural insight and an immersion into the wild surroundings. Another outpost, Sundy Praia, is set within what was once part of Príncipe’s second-largest cocoa plantation on the remote northwest tip and hosts guests in tented villas backing the golden shores on the remote northwest tip of the island. —Lauren Burris Hill.

Go for: ancient treasures and contemporary culture by the sea.

Villa Kahina, an intimate guesthouse that opened in September in Tunis.

In the blue and white village of Sidi Bou Saïd, the six-room Villa Kahina offers views of the Mediterranean.

Designated 2027’s Arab Capital of Tourism, this languid North African city now pulses with the energy of a new generation of Tunisian creatives and entrepreneurs. Events planned in the historic Medina range from TedX Pasha Street talks and musical retreats to artisanal workshops, many organized by the beloved Dar Ben Gacem boutique hotel and cultural hub, which will also host a rooftop event for August’s solar eclipse. Across the Medina, near the Great Mosque of Zitouna, Dar Ben Turkia's early 2026 opening expands the luxury-hotel options that preserve the area’s history. The elegant eight-suite hideaway has an in-house hammam and spa, so it doubles as a wellness retreat in the heart of the Medina. Beyond the medieval city’s labyrinths, the sun-kissed ruins of ancient Carthage spill toward the coast. Anchoring these archaeological riches is the Carthage National Museum, slated to reopen by year-end after an eight-year overhaul. For more contemporary treasures, head downhill to the city’s leading art gallery, Selma Feriani, which in 2027 will exhibit major Tunisian artists Mohamed Amine Hamouda and Rafik El Kamel.

Nearby, sleek seaside city La Marsa gives way to the historically working-class neighborhood of Bhar Lazreg, where artists and makers have been repurposing spaces. Anchors like the B7L9 Art Centre (built by and for the area’s community), and Phosphor Creative District—showcasing local talent who specialize in everything from fine art to design—are transforming the area into a meeting place for artists, demonstrating why the neighborhood has become known as one of Tunis’s coolest. Meanwhile, fashionable La Marsa remains a firm favorite with the stylish set, and mid-2026 restaurant openings like Oto, a Japanese izakaya, and Sujet, a hybrid café and design store, keep things fresh. When you’re ready for a break, make your way up the coast to Birdie at The Clubhouse in Gammarth, which opened in August 2026, or south to Villa Kahina, an intimate guesthouse that began welcoming guests in September. Perched on the forested edge of the iconic blue and white village of Sidi Bou Saïd, this whitewashed six-room sanctuary with sweeping Mediterranean views feels almost untouched by time. —Lee Middleton.

Go for: a host of fresh hotels from which to experience some of Africa’s best beaches.

Beyond its beaches, Zanzibar is set to welcome two latest luxury properties: Anantara Zanzibar Resort and Residences in 2027, followed by Four Seasons Resort Zanzibar at Pongwe in 2028.

Recent findings suggest that most visitors arrive in Zanzibar with postcard perfection already in mind—turquoise shallows, swaying palms, and dhows tipping into the sunset—but the island’s enduring drawcard is still Stone Town: a UNESCO-listed tangle of coral-rag limestone alleys, carved Omani doors, and clove-scented air, where Africa, Arabia, and India have intersected for centuries. In 2027 Zanzibar gets its most serious branded hotel wave yet with the 181-key Anantara Zanzibar Resort & Residences on the north coast, and in 2028 it will welcome, the 60-villa Four Seasons Resort Zanzibar at Pongwe, widely regarded as the loveliest beach on the east coast. The latter is a short flight from the brand’s Serengeti lodge and has been built with a bush-and-beach pairing in mind. The freshest energy is homegrown, though, and it has moved away from the overdeveloped north. In Jambiani, on the sunrise-facing southeast coast, the seven-villa Ma’a Salama (“go in peace”) opened in mid-2026 as a nonprofit that doubles as a hospitality school, training island youth in exchange for a year’s free education. Ma’a Salama’s spacious villas are named for spices and are cooled by bioclimatic design rather than air-conditioning, and four are crowned with rooftop teahouses, designed in Stone Town’s famous Emerson’s teahouses. On the quiet southwest coast at Kizimkazi, Kizikula is the antithesis of a resort: no sign, no jetty, just a jungly pathway leading to what feels more like a private home or artist’s enclave than a hotel. At low tide, guests access the beach through a secret gap in the coral cliff. Designed by Mumbai’s Case Design, its coral-limestone rooms sit in wild permaculture gardens. In 2026 the resort added 19 rooms, and in December it will open a newly introduced rooftop sunset bar and a three-floor wellness center, where treatments incorporate ingredients like Zanzibari cinnamon, turmeric, and cardamom. As of October 2026 Airlink flies the first-ever nonstop route between Cape Town and Zanzibar, with low-cost FlySafair rumored to be expanding its regular Johannesburg service to include Cape Town too. The UK gets its own first direct link in November 2027, courtesy of TUI Airways’s Gatwick service, along with a direct London flight from Air Tanzania. —Jane Broughton.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mein Schiff 3 will resume its sailings later this month, TUI shared in an update.

In a recent development, following repair work at Lloyd Werft’s Bremerhaven pier, the ship will embark on its scheduled four-night cruise from Bremerhaven to Kiel via Oslo on Nov. 28.

“We know that many of our guests have been eagerly looking forward to their upcoming voyage. We’re all the more delighted to be able to welcome them back aboard Mein Schiff 3, and we wish all our guests a wonderful trip,” TUI noted.

The ship was damaged on October 25, when it collided with a container ship while leaving Bremerhaven in stormy conditions.

Two cruises were canceled as a result, the first one being a cruise to the Canaries, where the ship was headed when the collision occurred.

The second one was the “Enchanting Norway” cruise that was scheduled for  November 14-28, canceled because TUI judged repairs would take longer than planned.

Another bill to release Epstein files headed to House floor

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that massie will force another vote on releasing files in the Jeffrey Epstein case.
  • Recent findings suggest that as Rep.
  • A discharge petition led by Massie aimed at extracting more files from the Justice Department has now received enough support to force a vote on the House floor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that massie will force another vote on releasing files in the Jeffrey Epstein case. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call file photo).

Recent findings suggest that as Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., enters his final weeks in Congress, he is one step closer to another vote on legislation related to the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

A discharge petition led by Massie aimed at extracting more files from the Justice Department has now received enough support to force a vote on the House floor.

According to recent reports, rep. John Garamendi, D-Calif., was the decisive 218th signature on the discharge petition, a procedural tool allowing rank-and-file House members to register their support for a piece of legislation and circumvent leadership to force a vote. Massie and other supporters of the effort say the bill is a bid for transparency.

Earlier this week, Massie mentioned his pitch to his colleagues was simple.

“They could be a hero if they sign it,” he said, as he chased down the final two signatures as the House returned from recess on Monday. Rep. Adam Smith, D-Wash., signed just before Garamendi.

Massie’s time left in office is ticking down after a challenger backed by President Donald Trump ousted him in his GOP primary earlier this year.

Industry observers note that the petition marks the second push led by Massie to require the release of the Epstein files. Last fall, Massie and Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., led a discharge petition on a bill dubbed the Epstein Files Transparency Act, which directed the Justice Department to publicly release documents in its possession related to Epstein and his associate Ghislaine Maxwell.

The bill passed the House by a vote of 427-1 last November, and in the Senate a few days later. Trump signed the measure shortly afterward.

In a statement this summer, Massie remarked he believes the Justice Department is still withholding more than 3 million files that it is required to release under the November 2025 law and is “maintaining heavy redactions” on others.

Sources indicate that the latest bill would allow state attorneys general, local prosecutors and victims to sue the federal government for withholding such documents. It would also allow victims to privately view unredacted versions of any records that mention them.

Now that the newly introduced petition has reached 218 signatures, it must sit for seven legislative days before being called up by anyone who signed it. Last time around, Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., scheduled a House vote on the initial Epstein bill before that ripening period was over, saying it was a foregone conclusion that the legislation would reach the floor.

Other Republicans who have signed on to the petition this year include Reps. Nancy Mace, R-S.C.; Ralph Norman, R-S.C., and Brian Fitzpatrick, R-Pa., none of whom will be returning next Congress. Rep. Lauren Boebert, R-Colo., backed the initial effort last fall, but her name did not appear on the petition this time.

Sources indicate that allies of the issue in Congress have faced pushback from Trump. While the president suggested during his 2024 reelection campaign that he was open to declassifying some Epstein documents, Trump then shifted gears, calling them a “hoax.”.

Sources indicate that “Once you get to 218, you can never sign it," Massie said. "There's nobody left, no spots left. It goes straight to the floor, and then you can vote for it. But you were never part of the group that actually got it to the floor.".

Southeast Asia’s Coolest Newly introduced Hotels Are Eco-Conscious Tented Camps

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, there's something exhilarating about bedding down under canvas: the fresh breeze drifting in, the sounds of distant rumbles and nearby rustling, and an untouched landscape unfurling right at the foot of your bed. For decades those experiences have been synonymous with the classic safari lodges pitched up around East and Southern Africa, but a fresh generation of small-scale camps are giving the concept a Southeast Asian spin. These intimate and wonderfully wild retreats, including one in a remote corner of northwest Cambodia and another in the forest-cloaked mountains of central Vietnam, trade the region's usual resort formula for a lighter footprint and, with it, a much deeper connection to its jungle perch.

A boat excursion on an underground river inside Vietnam’s largest cave network.

According to recent reports, in the shade of the camel-hump limestone karst formations of central Vietnam's Phong Nha–Ké Bàng National Park, Auko Eco recently opened as a plush base to wind down between mud-splattered mountain hikes and scrambles within the world's largest cave system. The camp's 30 canvas suites, each with mod cons like air-conditioning and an open-air bathtub, are built from local bamboo and timber reclaimed from fishing boats, and they are clustered so that most of the plots' native plant cover remains intact. Riverside yoga classes, hydrotherapy, and sound-healing sessions in the on-site meditation cave soothe minds and muscles after a day in the wild.

One of the 15 safari-style tents at Siempang Forest Lodge.

Inside one of the guest tents at Siempang Forest Lodge.

The songs of Cambodia's most elusive bird species make up the soundtrack to a stay at Siempang Forest Lodge, a camp of 15 safari-style tents on stilted decks that opened last fall in the heart of a 330,577-acre wildlife sanctuary of the same name. While there's a pool, a simple spa, and a well-stocked bar for sundowners, the camp's conservation-minded backstory is the real draw. Guests can join local rangers on forest walks and birding excursions to spot critically endangered critters such as wild bantengs (a species of cattle), Siamese crocodiles, and giant ibis, and learn firsthand how tourism helps revive and safeguard one of the country's last great swaths of wilderness.

At the entrance to Vietnam’s Hang So’n Đoòng, one of the largest natural caves in the world.

Over the last few years, Koh Phangan has been shedding its Full Moon Party reputation by swapping the usual days of debauchery for holidays with a more mindful tilt. When Kaia, draped over a palm-heavy peninsula on the island's quiet northeast, opens, it will embrace that go-slow shift with 35 tented suites furnished with floorboards from reclaimed teak and decor from upcycled materials. Communal meals that center on homegrown produce cooked over an open fire will be served at the beach club and the breezy restaurant up the hill, while a stable of activities like ceramic workshops, guided foraging trips, and breath work sessions will tap into the local creative community.

How I Got My Visa to France

📅 16 Feb 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1973 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nomadicmatt

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that I’ve been in love with France ever since my first trip to Bordeaux in 2010.
  • But that love became an obsession when, after Bordeaux, I stepped out of the Paris metro and onto the Champs-Élysées.
  • Since then, Paris has had a firm grip on my heart.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that I’ve been in love with France ever since my first trip to Bordeaux in 2010. Friends I had met back in Thailand indicated me around the area and introduced me to French culture. It was my first time in France and I loved the food, the wine, and the people.

But that love became an obsession when, after Bordeaux, I stepped out of the Paris metro and onto the Champs-Élysées. The lights, the energy, the mystique! There was magic in the air. I felt like I had known the city my entire life and I was simply returning home.

Since then, Paris has had a firm grip on my heart. Over the years, I spent countless visits exploring France and Paris in particular. I’ve run tours in the city and I spent a few months living there in 2019.

Last August, after yet another sojourn, I thought to myself, “What if I moved back?”.

I was growing a bit tired of the NYC dating scene, the rising cost of living, and felt like, creatively, I was in a rut. With AI coming for creators like me and the industry changing, I was a little lost on what, career-wise, would come next.

And Paris seemed like the best place to go.

Recent findings suggest that it’s cheaper than NYC, I had friends there already, I’ve always wanted to learn French, it would make a great base for exploring Europe, and I could start writing my next book there. There’s nothing like a change in scenery to get the creativity flowing!

But the question remained: how do you move to France?

After all, they don’t have a digital nomad visa, and you’re limited to three months if you visit on your regular Schengen tourist visa.

Well, it turns out that it’s not actually that hard. (And while I can only speak for Americans, I suspect the criteria are similar for Canadians, Aussies, Kiwis, and other “developed” nations.).

If you want to move to France, you have four main options:.

In a recent development, the student visa is pretty straightforward. You need to enroll in a full-time university program and show you have enough funds to support yourself (around 600 Euros per month). A friend is presently there on this visa, as she is doing a nine-month intensive French program to become fluent. You still have to apply for the visa, but if you’re enrolled in an accredited school, you’ll likely get approved. Another benefit to this visa is that you can work part-time on it!

But this visa is contingent on being in school, so if you leave or quit, it’s voided. However, when you are done, you can change this to a “job seeker” visa, which can give you up to another six months in France (or more depending on how long your program was).

Sources indicate that I thought about applying for the entrepreneur visa, but the application process is pretty complex and can take months to be approved. You have to set up your business in France — and that is a lot of paperwork. You have to show that your business makes money, has clients (at least one of them being French), and can support you full-time (you have to make at least the French minimum wage). They will scrutinize your assets and financials a lot and you’ll need to register your business in France and pay French taxes.

It has been revealed that additionally, France offers a talent visa. If you’re an expert in your field (with verifiable accreditations and accolades), this could be a good visa to apply for, especially if you plan to stay in France for a long time and want to physically work there. But, again, you’ll need to have some source of income and plan to do physical business in France. If you’re not an academic but someone in the arts, you have to show how you are going to add to the “culture of France” in some way.

While I would meet the requirements for both those visas, the process for either would have been time-consuming, and, since I’m not sure France is going to be my forever home, I decided not to go through that process.

Industry observers note that so I went with the long-term visitor visa, officially called VLS-TS visiteur. This allows me to stay up to 12 months in France and is renewable in the country. It does come with a lot of restrictions, however: I can’t physically work here and I am not allowed into the French social welfare system.

It’s also the visa a lot of Americans (and most retirees) are coming in on. If you have passive income or retirement savings and just want to live in France, this is a good option for you. It allows you to set up a bank account and it can be renewed pretty much indefinitely.

The paperwork for this visa (which I’ll get into in a bit) essentially comes down to whether or not you can support yourself. French authorities want to make sure you won’t be a burden on the system.

According to recent reports, my biggest question centered around whether or not I could “work” on this visa. A lot of creators and digital nomads are applying for — and getting — this visa.

But remember: you aren’t allowed to work on this visa so how are you going to work if you can’t work?

So let me take a moment to talk about “work” from a legal standpoint.

As I mentioned, there’s no digital nomad visa that allows you to work in France. And the French tax office noted last July that remote work is considered taxable — but there are no official laws that say so. That’s just their opinion and there’s been no progress in codifying that opinion. In fact, my visa doesn’t even come with a tax number, so I can’t be taxed. I couldn’t pay taxes even if I wanted to.

The visa office asks how you’ll support yourself when you are in France and one of the sources of income they accept is “income from work.” I was very open that my means of support would be the income from this blog and my books.

The system there really hasn’t caught up to remote work. It still defines “work” as something you do physically that could take away a job from a French person.

So could I run walking tours in Paris? Nope. Could you work at a café? Nope.

But does writing this blog post count as work? After all, no one is paying for it. It’s a free resource. Does going to a café to work on the next great American novel count? What about my weekly newsletter that has affiliate links (that generate income) in it? Is writing that considered work?

The gray area is considerable, so the best thing to do is to talk to a lawyer. I recommend Daniel Tostado (yes, that’s his real name), one of the biggest American-French immigration lawyers in Paris. He has a huge law firm and regularly meets with government officials to clarify the rules on this. He gave me some solid advice.

Recent findings suggest that for this long-term visitor visa, the application process is pretty easy. You go to the French government website, fill out your application, take the application number to the TLScontact website, and make an appointment. (France outsources the appointment process to this company, which then sends everything to the French consulate for approval.).

The main things you’ll want to demonstrate are that you have accommodation for 90 days on your application and enough income to support yourself. They just want to make sure you aren’t going to be a burden on the system. I went overboard. Here’s what I brought to my appointment:.

In a recent development, I didn’t need the second bank account, tax returns, or W-2 (they weren’t required) but the woman at the appointment said the more proof you had the better and it wouldn’t hurt. And another friend who got this visa didn’t bring anything beyond what was asked in the application form. But I wanted to take no chances!

It has been revealed that at the appointment, the staff double-checks your paperwork, takes your biometric data, collects the fees, and then sends your passport to the embassy for processing. Officially, it takes up to 15 days to process your visa, but everyone I know seems to get it back within a week.

It has been revealed that the worst part was not knowing if you are approved until your passport is returned. While you can track the progress of your application, you don’t know the verdict until your passport is back in your hands. While I was waiting (and anxiously spiraling), I looked on Reddit and found that most denials were for lack of income or issues with their accommodation, which seem to be the two most important things to have perfect on your application.

Once you get your visa back, you can enter France any time after the start date. After you enter, you have 90 days to register your visa with the state (they give you a little QR code with instructions). This allows you to “officially” be on this long-term visa. (It’s a more paperwork kind of thing.).

Once that is done, there’s nothing else to do and you can stay in France (and Europe) until your visa expires!

So, if you’re considering moving to France, these are your options. But, as always, I’m not a lawyer and this is not legal advice. In regard to work and other issues or questions, it’s vital that you seek legal counsel and get their expert opinion!

Book Your Accommodation You can book your hostel with Hostelworld as they have the biggest inventory and best deals. If you want to stay somewhere other than a hostel, use Booking.com as they consistently return the cheapest rates for guesthouses and cheap hotels.

  • The move clears the way for Senate Ethics Chairman James Lankford, R-Okla., to use his seniority to ascend to ranking Republican on the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, which Paul at the moment chairs, and touches off several other shifts at the top of other committees.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., leaves the Senate Republicans’ lunch in the Capitol on Tuesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call) (Bill Clark CQ Roll Call).

It has been revealed that sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., unveiled Wednesday he plans to serve as the top Republican on the Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee when Democrats take control of Congress next year.

The move clears the way for Senate Ethics Chairman James Lankford, R-Okla., to use his seniority to ascend to ranking Republican on the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, which Paul at the moment chairs, and touches off several other shifts at the top of other committees.

The move fit in with Sen. Lisa Murkowski’s bid to use her seniority to succeed Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins, R-Maine, as top Republican on the Appropriations panel. If Paul did not go to the top spot on HELP, Murkowski, R-Alaska, would be next in line for that committee in the next Congress.

Recent findings suggest that murkowski is second in seniority on Appropriations to Collins, who was defeated for reelection. But she faces a potential challenge from Sen. Jerry Moran, R-Kan., who is next in line behind her.

Paul mentioned in a press release that he plans to bring the same approach to the HELP Committee as he did as chairman of Homeland, where he said he “challenged entrenched bureaucracies, forced federal officials to answer for their actions, and pulled back the curtain on what Washington tried to keep hidden.”.

Sources indicate that he cited calling Dr. Anthony Fauci before the committee to probe the former federal health official’s role in pandemic-related shutdowns and the origin of the COVID-19 virus, and releasing thousands of pages of pandemic-related documents. The panel voted in August to hold Fauci in criminal contempt of Congress for declining to answer questions about the pandemic during a highly charged hearing.

Related: Fauci could face criminal contempt charge following panel vote.

Paul, an ophthalmologist, remarked at HELP he will “stand against efforts to put Washington between Americans and their doctors, their children’s schools, and their paychecks.” He predicted “a rush toward socialism unlike anything we have seen” when the Democrat-controlled Congress convenes in January.

In a recent development, lankford, in a separate statement, confirmed his interest in becoming the ranking member of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee. In many areas, he said, the panel can work in a bipartisan manner, and over the past decade he “worked across the aisle to improve emergency communications in federal buildings, strengthen the United States Postal Service, increase federal cybersecurity preparedness, government transparency, and the use of artificial intelligence.”.

It has been revealed that but he added that his job also would be to “push back on a [Democratic] majority that goes too far . . . Oversight is responsible, but obstruction is unacceptable.”.

Lankford said he would work together with the likely committee chair, Sen. Maggie Hassan, D-N.H., “when we can agree and be a fierce opposition if there is an attempt to undercut our nation’s security.”.

Debuting in late 2028, the PC6 class Ocean Spirit is an expedition vessel developed specifically for the cruise line thanks to a deal inked between Poseidon and United Waterways and its ocean division Ocean Advice this summer.

Poseidon has now shared that the 120-meter-long ship will be able to accommodate 160 guests in suites across seven categories: Window, Balcony, Promenade, Deluxe, Captain’s, Panorama and Owner’s.

Beyond suites, the ship will feature public spaces designed to complement the journey, including lounges, dining spaces, observation decks and wellness facilities.

Noting that this marks a latest chapter for the manufacturer, the cruise line remarked that the Ocean Spirit carries the ethos of Poseidon Expeditions forward as a new expression of the spirit of exploration that has guided it from the beginning.
